A finite <ACCENT_0001>tale morphism is locally isomorphic to a disjoint union
of isomorphisms, see
<ACCENT_0002>tale Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0001>.
Thus (2) implies (1). Conversely, if <MATH_0001> is finite locally
constant, then there exists an <ACCENT_0003>tale covering <MATH_0002> such that
<MATH_0003> is representable by <MATH_0004> finite <ACCENT_0004>tale.
Arguing exactly as in the proof of
Descent, Lemma <REF_0002>
we obtain a descent datum for schemes <MATH_0005> relative to
<MATH_0006> (details omitted). This descent datum is effective for
example by Descent, Lemma <REF_0003>
and the resulting morphism of schemes <MATH_0007> is finite <ACCENT_0005>tale
by Descent, Lemmas <REF_0004> and
<REF_0005>.

Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme.

<STRUCT_0002> Let <MATH_0002> be a map
of locally constant sheaves of sets on <MATH_0003>.
If <MATH_0004> is finite locally constant, there exists an
<ACCENT_0001>tale covering <MATH_0005> such that
<MATH_0006> is the map of constant sheaves associated to
a map of sets.
<STRUCT_0003> Let <MATH_0007> be a map
of locally constant sheaves of abelian groups on <MATH_0008>.
If <MATH_0009> is finite locally constant, there exists an <ACCENT_0002>tale
covering <MATH_0010> such that <MATH_0011> is the map of
constant abelian sheaves associated to a map of abelian groups.
<STRUCT_0004> Let <MATH_0012> be a ring.
Let <MATH_0013> be a map
of locally constant sheaves of <MATH_0014>-modules on <MATH_0015>.
If <MATH_0016> is of finite type, then there exists an <ACCENT_0003>tale covering
<MATH_0017> such that <MATH_0018> is the map of constant
sheaves of <MATH_0019>-modules associated to a map of <MATH_0020>-modules.
